verdict.rationale: Meilisearch documents API keys plus tenant tokens, which are short-lived, scoped credentials derived from an API key. Tenant tokens embed filter rules that apply to every search, so a credential handed to an agent can be limited to a subset of data. However, the evidence only shows this scoping for search reads. Nothing shows per-action or per-index permission scoping on API keys, or how credentials are scoped for the native MCP server an agent would use. Missing for 10: documented action/index-level API key permissions, least-privilege credential guidance for agents or the MCP endpoint, scoping of write operations, independent or hands-on corroboration.
